bug_semantics: dw_edma_pcie_probe() casts pci_device_id.driver_data to struct dw_edma_pcie_data * and treats that pointer as the eDMA controller-layout template with no NULL check. The static id_table always supplies &snps_edda_data, but a device bound dynamically via sysfs (PCI new_id/bind with driver_data=0) reaches probe with a NULL template. At the CVE fix point the first use is memcpy(vsec_data, pdata, sizeof(struct dw_edma_pcie_data)), a NULL pointer dereference; the original 2019 probe already crashed earlier by reading pdata->rg_bar/ll_bar/dt_bar in pcim_iomap_regions(). A local actor who can bind the driver can oops the kernel.
flaw_origin: The missing NULL guard was written with the driver itself. 41aaff2a2ac01c5f5415f9de9cd7015ac2b8d569 (Gustavo Pimentel, Synopsys, 2019-06-04) added drivers/dma/dw-edma/dw-edma-pcie.c and first implemented dw_edma_pcie_probe() as pdata = (void *)pid->driver_data followed by unconditional use of pdata fields. 1aef6ffe999eec7b7fdcfad7ffef9c157727ffcb later dropped const and memcpy'd the template into a mutable VSEC overlay, changing the first crash site but not introducing the unchecked driver_data trust. Immediate parent 1f418f46503d72594bbe6407d97fd2ae1ce15ee6 has no dw-edma-pcie.c.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: CVE-2026-72147 is a published Linux CNA kernel CVE (not withdrawn/rejected), matching GHSA-47f2-6xxj-8w97. dw_edma_pcie_probe() trusts pci_device_id.driver_data as a dw_edma_pcie_data template. Sysfs dynamic bind can deliver driver_data=0, so pdata is NULL and the kernel NULL-dereferences—historically on pdata->rg_bar in pcim_iomap_regions(), and at the CVE era on memcpy(vsec_data, pdata, sizeof(...)). The fix is a three-line reject (`if (!pdata) return -ENODEV`) before enabling the device. BIC choice: the smallest public commit that first wrote that unchecked template use is 41aaff2a2ac01c5f5415f9de9cd7015ac2b8d569, which introduced the new PCIe glue file.
